question: Are distinct host-return records always new image evidence with a known exposure time?
scope: All448 saved PMPose keypoints; raw upright PNG frames35..61 only; source AVI verification at35,36,58,59,60,61; no network/model/optimization or observation changes
timestamp_warning: host_return_timestamp_ns is recorded after VideoCapture.read() returns; it is not a sensor exposure timestamp or hardware synchronization error.
selection_identity: Existing _read_capture_times verifies sequence order and selected frame IDs against source CSV; all448 retained

code_evidence.frame_id: realtime_app/pose_app/stereo_camera.py:_capture_loop; frame_id=self.captured_count; increment once per successful validated read
code_evidence.estimator_time: realtime_app/tools/run_stereo_pva_baseline.py:_read_capture_times; mean left/right host-return ns minus first pair
code_evidence.pixel_gate: realtime_app/pose_app/smplh_motion_tracker.py:_supported_pixels; finite/bounds/score/epipolar only; no image-content or exposure-ID input
code_evidence.extraction: realtime_app/walker_tools/stereo/prepare_continuous_stereo_segment.py:main; frame-ID to CSV AVI-position mapping and sequential decoding

limits: Exact saved image equality proves repeated image content, not a specific hardware/driver cause or actual exposure ID.
Whole448 keypoint equality is a cheap screen; only frames35..61 are verified against image pixels.
Host skew cannot certify exposure synchronization; no sensor timestamp/exposure counter is stored in the inspected CSV schemas.
No frame is deleted/replaced and no nominal30fps is substituted.
This identifies a data-time and independence problem; it does not yet measure its causal effect on ankle height or justify blaming events37/59 on duplicates alone.

existing_trace_on_repeated_content.scope: Reads existing exact-baseline trace only; no counterfactual replay
existing_trace_on_repeated_content.interpretation: All8 repeated-content updates lower mean ankle height locally; they are not the two direct rise steps. Their counterfactual influence on covariance/history is unmeasured.

conclusion: Distinct read counters and host-return times demonstrably include repeated image content. Current update treats every valid supplied pixel record as another measurement; independence and physical derivative time are not established. The inspected local image repeats occur before37 and after59, while35->37 and58->59 contain new image content; duplicate content alone is not a demonstrated source of the two rise events.

observation_semantics.source_scope: Existing raw export fields plus inspected local current source/config; no historical Docker runtime revision is independently certified by these checks
observation_semantics.extra_channel_conclusion: PMPose23 merges COCO/AIC/MPII; channels17..22 are torso/head landmarks, not toe/heel landmarks. Current first17 selection matches this schema.
observation_semantics.score_contract: Local PMPose-b config has freeze_oks=False. MultiHead.predict preserves heatmap score as keypoints_conf, exports predicted OKS as keypoint_scores, and exports visibility/presence separately. api concatenates keypoint_scores as xy third channel. Do not interpret it as visibility probability, pixel standard deviation, or calibrated confidence.

current_tracker_score_use.interpretation: Finite/bounds/score and stereo gate decide support; admitted points use uniform pixel_sigma8 before residual-dependent Huber downweighting. No score-to-variance calibration and no separate visibility/presence field enter this tracker.

observation_semantics.event_interpretation: Right knee crosses35px support gate36->37 and58->59 while raw scores remain high. Right-knee visibility is also high at these events; low predicted visibility is not supported as its cause. Right-view hip scores remain high while their separate visibility can be low, exposing different scalar meanings without establishing true anatomical visibility.
